records.title: Biological Control Systems Engineering
records.text: BIOEN 438 Biological Control Systems Engineering (3) Introduces proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller design for closed loop systems in biomedical applications. Focuses on developing design skills with modest emphasis on theory. Key skills taught: setting control objectives, building an in silico testbed, PID design using root locus plots, and control tuning. Final project is a control design for a biomedical pathway of the student's choosing. Prerequisite: either MATH 135, MATH 207, or AMATH 351; recommended: BIOL 200; CSE 160 or AMATH 301; and BIOEN 336 or equivalent.

records.title: Contemporary Light Microscopy
records.text: BIOEN 445 Contemporary Light Microscopy (3) Introduction to the practical and theoretical foundations of light microscopy and advanced optical techniques used to study biological systems. Topics include the physics of light, physiology of the eye, photodetectors, bright field, dark field, and phase contrast microscopy; optical trapping; interference, polarization, and fluorescence; confocal and super-resolution microscopy; and image processing and machine learning strategies. Recommended: electromagnetism (PHYS 122 or equivalent); wave physics (PHYS 123 or equivalent); differential equations (either MATH 207, AMATH 351, or equivalent); and introductory biology (BIOL 200 or equivalent).

Introduces principles of sound propagation, reflection, transmission, refraction, absorption, and bioeffects due to tissue interaction. Covers clinical applications, technology, and techniques and tools in modern therapeutic ultrasound procedures and devices. Discusses current challenges and opportunities in therapeutic ultrasound. records.title: Therapeutic Drug Delivery Systems
records.text: BIOEN 491 Therapeutic Drug Delivery Systems (3) Introduces the principles, strategies, and materials in controlled drug delivery systems. Covers fundamentals of drug delivery, including physiology, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, drug diffusion and permeation, and biologics. Discusses biomaterials for drug delivery and controlled release strategies for various delivery routes. Includes guest lectures on special topics in industry. Offered: jointly with CHEM E 491.
